what: Mistake: queued the records-history steps naming their dependencies in words ('depends on job 7 part 2'), but athena plan reads dependencies only from job ids in the text, so the plan put job 8 (remove records/ from main) ahead of the cutover; a drain would have run them in that order. Also wrote acceptance inline, which plan does not parse, so all seven were held.
why: The request format athena plan parses (acceptance as bullets, dependencies as job ids) should be documented where requests are written, and athena ask --later could warn when a request names a dependency in words or has no parsable acceptance.
